source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
The thesis includes a monthly rainfall record table for Preah Sihanouk (Sihanoukville) city covering 1988-1993, used to assess the site's suitability for coconut. Reading the scanned, rotated table with full confidence at the individual-cell level was not possible, but the annual totals are legible enough to characterize the climate: total annual rainfall across these six years falls in roughly the 3,000-4,200 mm range, with the wettest months concentrated from around May through October (the southwest monsoon period) and a drier stretch in the early months of the year (January-March showing the lowest monthly figures in every year of the table).

This level of rainfall is consistent with Sihanoukville's coastal, high-rainfall climate and was cited in the thesis as favorable for coconut, which tolerates and benefits from consistently high rainfall as long as drainage is adequate. Precise month-by-month figures from this table are not reproduced here because the scan's small, rotated numerals could not be transcribed with confidence; a future session with access to a clearer copy of this source could re-extract the full monthly table.
